extracted.intended_audience: Korean Intellectual Property Office examiners and patent applicants handling foreign-language applications
extracted.subtask_description: Examination and procedural guidance for handling foreign‑language patent applications (including mistranslation corrections, divisional/converted applications, and domestic priority claims) in Korea. Covers what constitutes new matter, how to evaluate corrected translations, prior‑art searching, timing, and formal requirements for special applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscription of introduction of new matter beyond the Korean translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there were no errors in the Korean translations but the Korean translations have become different from the foreign language specification due to unnecessary and irrelevant correction, a rejection shall be issued on the ground of introduction of new matter beyond the Korean translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example sequence: (1) foreign-language application at filing (A), (2) specification deemed amended after submission of Korean translations (A->A), (3) Korean translations corrected (A->B), (4) specification un-amended. If Korean translations were correct originally, unnecessary correction that creates divergence from the foreign-language spec may trigger rejection for new matter beyond the Korean translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscription of introduction of new matter beyond the foreign language specification and the Korean translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a specification for examination is amended beyond the scope of the corrected Korean translations and the foreign language specification, a rejection shall be issued on the ground of introduction of new matter beyond the foreign language specification and the Korean translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: (1) foreign-language spec at filing (A), (2) spec deemed amended after submission of Korean translations (A->B), (3) Korean translations corrected (B->C), (4) specification amended (B->D). If the specification for examination (D) is beyond corrected Korean translations (C) and the foreign-language specification (A), it constitutes new matter. Applicant should correct wrong correction of mistranslation (C->A) and amend specification for examination accordingly (D->A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of correction of a mistranslation is not by itself grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a mistranslation is corrected, appropriateness and inappropriateness thereof shall not constitute reasons for rejection or reasons for amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should not reject or order amendment solely because they consider a corrected translation to be inappropriate; substantive evaluation focuses on formal grounds (e.g., new matter), not on subjective views of 'appropriateness'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary explanation requirement for correction of mistranslation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documentary materials accompanied by a statement of correction of a mistranslation do not explain reasons for correction or where reasons for correction are not sufficiently described so that appropriateness of correction is hard to evaluate, amendment shall be ordered on the ground of insufficient reasons for correction, and the appropriateness of correction shall be evaluated after translation errors are resolved through amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendment cannot relieve insufficient reasons for correction, correction of the mistranslation itself shall be invalidated. Examples: (1) no objective explanation why pre-amendment translation is unreasonable and post-amendment translation is reasonable; (2) vague claims that error arose from interpretation/context without sufficient description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Korean translations in prior-art searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a foreign language specification and Korean translations thereof are generally identical, it is sufficiently enough only to search the Korean translations when a foreign-language application is searched as prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is doubt that the Korean translations differ from the foreign-language specification, the scope of search shall be expanded to include the foreign-language specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to review foreign-language specification for enlarged concept of novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a foreign-language patent application serves as prior art for the enlarged concept of novelty, the foreign-language specification should finally be reviewed even though search may be based on the Korean specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although initial searching may rely on Korean translations laid open to public inspection, the ultimate novelty assessment must consider the foreign-language specification itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of notice of grounds for rejection when citing foreign-language prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a foreign-language patent application is cited as 'prior art for enlarged concept of novelty', a notice of grounds for rejection shall be stated in such a way that the foreign-language specification corresponding to the Korean specification constitute reasons for rejection, with reference to the Korean specification (which are amended based on the Korean translations) that have been laid open to public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices should identify the corresponding foreign-language text but may refer to the publicly available Korean specification (as amended) as basis for the stated reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's response when applicant disputes disclosure in foreign-language specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a notice of grounds for rejection is issued based on a foreign-language patent application and the applicant can argue that the invention under examination is not disclosed in the foreign-language specification, the reasons for rejection shall be overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant shows that the foreign-language spec does not disclose the claimed subject matter, the examiner must withdraw the rejection. Separately, if new matter is found in the pending foreign-language application, a notice shall be issued on ground of introduction of new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of first-to-file rule when prior-filed application contains new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an invention claimed in the prior-filed application includes new matter beyond the foreign-language specification, the claimed invention cannot be relied on in issuing a rejection based on Article 36(1)-(3) of the Patent Act; new matter introduced in a prior-filed application claim cannot be a bar to a later application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same principle applies to foreign-language patent applications to conform to the first-to-file rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic approach: treat foreign-language applications as regular domestic applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign-language application is considered as a regular domestic application; divisional, converted, or domestic priority-claim applications shall be permitted accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For divisional/converted applications and domestic priority claims, requirements are evaluated on the basis of the foreign-language specification. However, because foreign-language specs commonly coincide with Korean translations, examiners may depend on Korean translations when determining retroactive filing dates or similar issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application substantive requirement — scope of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application shall be within the scope of the matters described in the original specification or drawings of the parent application; inventions of the divisional must all have been disclosed in the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner determines whether the divisional invention is explicitly described or obviously recognized as implicitly described; refer to 'Scope of Amendment' for methods. If any invention in the divisional is not contained in the parent, the divisional is invalid or has grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application validity basis — original specification/drawings control
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification or drawings that form the basis of validity for a divisional application is the specification or drawings originally attached to the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if an invention was deleted from an amended parent specification, that originally disclosed invention remains eligible for a divisional. Conversely, inventions newly added to the parent through amendments are not eligible for division because they were not originally disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application and double-filing/filing date effects
rubrics_metrics.description: When a divisional is filed it is deemed to have been filed when the parent was filed; if claims of the divisional are identical to those of the parent, questions of double-filing arise but the divisional shall be recognized and examined under Article 36(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same applies where claims become identical after amendments; substantive requirements must still be satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application formal filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application must be filed stating the purport of the division and indicating the parent application; filing is by attaching the specification and necessary documents to a written patent application in the prescribed form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the parent application is not indicated at filing, the divisional will not be recognized as legitimate. Except for obvious errors, amendments changing the indicated parent after filing are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application amendment of parent and use of evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally the applicant should amend the parent to differentiate its claims from those of the divisional; however, amendment of the parent is not required if divisional inventions are disclosed only in the description or drawings of the parent. Applicants may rely on evidential documents submitted for the parent if they state the intention to refer to those documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims for disclosure exception or priority must be made and evidential documents submitted by prescribed dates (e.g., within 30 days for disclosure exception, within 3 months for priority) from the divisional filing date. If evidential documents were submitted with the parent, the applicant should state intention to rely on them when filing the divisional; otherwise the examiner will request amendment for formal deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application timing and pending-parent requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application must be filed within statutory timeframes (various periods depending on case) and the parent application must be pending before KIPO at the time of filing the divisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parent has been invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or the decision to reject has become final and binding, a divisional cannot be filed. If filed on the day parent procedure terminates, the divisional is treated as filed while parent was pending. For foreign-language parent applications, a divisional cannot be permitted before submission of Korean translations of the parent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of divisional application on filing date — exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional generally retains the filing date of the parent application, but shall be deemed filed at its actual filing date in particular conditions where it would be unfair to grant the retroactive filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: when a divisional corresponds to 'another application' under Article 29(3) or similar provisions, or when new subject matter is added to the divisional, the retroactive benefit of the parent's filing date is denied for the new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converted application substantive and timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A converted application shall fall within the scope of matters described in the specification of the original application; when Korean translations have been submitted, examiners shall compare the Korean translations of the original with the specification and drawings of the converted application. A converted application cannot be filed before submission of Korean translations of the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a converted application is foreign-language, specifications amended based on Korean translations (not the foreign-language spec) are compared with the original application's specification to determine substantive requirements. Proscription of new matter is separately evaluated by comparing the converted application's spec and the amended specification for examination. Defects rectified through amendment based on Korean translations may legitimize the converted application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application with domestic priority claim — evaluation method
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects of an application claiming domestic priority to a foreign-language application shall be evaluated by comparing the Korean translations of the prior-filed application and the specification and drawings of the application claiming domestic priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Korean translations of the prior-filed application have not yet been filed when the domestic-priority application is filed, the examiner shall compare the prior-filed application's specification and drawings with those of the claiming application. Otherwise examination proceeds similarly to other foreign-language application cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: International patent applications filed in a foreign language — handling and new-matter determination
rubrics_metrics.description: International patent applications filed in a foreign language shall be basically handled identically with foreign-language patent applications; they may correct mistranslation based on the specification and drawings filed on the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An international patent application filed in a foreign language may be invalidated or rejected on the ground of introduction of new matter in the original text, and the determination shall be based on the specification submitted up to the international filing date.
